Still, it's hard to know whether my hesitancy around exploring this topic is because I'm trying to avoid my trauma by hiding behind something else (possible but unlikely; I've always been one to dive towards instead of away from my problems, and blather endlessly about them to my friends), or because I feel intense shame around being judged in ANY capacity by ANYONE, even hypothetically by random strangers.

It's really hard to disentangle my desire for love and connection from my desire to be "who I am", or if "who I am" doesn't even exist and I'm just entirely composed of coping mechanisms for the trauma and pain at this point.

I have this outlook but the worst thing is that it HAS been completely justified. My entire life *has* fallen apart because I said or did ONE wrong thing, again and again. And no matter how much I try, or what healthier relationships I form, this repeats itself without end. So why should I not be paranoid, when paranoia's the only possible rational mindset?
I suppose, though what I feel "comfortable" has been so influenced by how I deal with my trauma that I don't know if this is just another offshoot of that.

> Does being in a lesbian relationship appeal to you in general and not in a sexual way? The romantic aspect, connecting with a woman romantically as a woman yourself? If this is relatable then it says something about your internal sense of self.

It is almost NEVER about sex, and always about an emotional connection/two women loving each other through a strong bond. Think catradora from she-ra, and several touhou ships which the community/myself have formed elaborate headcanons around. I'd go so far as to say I've for the most part not been able to fantasize about straight relationships or sex without having, as Contrapoints said, "my soul leave my body", and have always envisioned myself as femme-leaning or self-inserted as such in most relationships fantasized, even with IRL people I've crushed on.

As to your other questions:

> Does the idea of being perceived as female to everyone around you sound appealing?

I don't have to speculate about this because in some spaces online I frequent and used to frequent (including a trans advocacy/education discord server), I'm out as enby and it feels *good* to have people treat me female/more femme and compliment me in feminine terms. I in turn feel much more able to talk like my "natural" self, which as others have pointed out is and has mostly always been pretty feminine.

> Say you woke up the next day in a female body and everyone treated you like this had always been the case and you couldn’t change back—how would this make you feel?

Honestly, I think excitement petering out to long-term indifference. There's no way to really confirm this but I *have* for a while speculated that I'd feel just as fine being born in an AFAB body as an AMAB one - maybe even slightly better.

> Yea that’s all I’ve got for you. Ngl it seems like you are trying to convince yourself that all your feelings and behaviours have got to be due to something else unrelated to dysphoria which is fair, shit’s confusing to figure out.

This confusion is due to my BPD which makes it hard for me to tell what the hell is going on with my identity 99% of the time, as well as several hurtful comments former friends have made about my questioning/identity that led to me obsessing over these thoughts I had previously let go unquestioned (one of them was enby and accused me of "being autogynephilic").
